title: server: a summary roll-up that arrives with a restart keeps reading null on stored rows with no announcement (follow-up of #34096)
body:
domain:server#5 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jUg7BKfRBcTPyMxbLh

Filing gate ③: area-directed (area S2 of seat domain:server#5). This is open question 1 of os-dev report 6906716209 on #34096 (PR #34282), ruled A there with this card as the follow-up.

## Today (with PR #34282)

A summary roll-up that an install door adds in a running process is materialised for the rows already stored (`materialiseAddedSummaries` at the end of `syncSchemas`). A roll-up that arrives with a restart is not:
- a code-defined app's new version, which boots with the new field;
- a marketplace install whose hot register failed and loaded at the next restart;
- a ledger entry rehydrated at `kernel:ready`.

`ObjectQLPlugin` seals the roll-ups served at `kernel:bootstrapped` as already computed, so those rows keep reading `null` until a child row is written, and nothing tells the operator. `os migrate summary-nulls` is the documented backfill for that path.

## Ask

At `kernel:bootstrapped`, announce NULL `count` / `sum` roll-up holes with a bounded sample read per object, the way `announceStoredExpressionHoles` does for stored expressions. Write nothing. Name the `os migrate summary-nulls` line that fills them. Measure the sample's boot cost on a showcase boot, and pin both cases: a hole is announced once, and a computed column announces nothing.

Not asked: persisting the computed set to walk it at boot (option B in the report). That adds a stored contract and a boot-time write, so it needs its own ruling.

Prior rulings read: area ruling on #34096 open question 1 (A, with this card as the follow-up).

Reader: domain:server (objectql summaries). Size S.
